title: A Songbook for the Promise
premise: August Halloran, a pastry chef drowning in debt and emotional armor, agrees to pose as the girlfriend of Theo Vance—a hotel heir whose family reunion demands a plus-one—to earn money for her failing café. What begins as a transactional arrangement deepens as Theo's family estate becomes the site of her dream expansion and the stage for his own quiet rebellion against a corrupting inheritance. When August discovers Theo's family intends to buy out her block and that his grandmother, the matriarch, orchestrated their meeting as a test of Theo's loyalty, she must choose between the café she's bled for and the man who taught her the heart isn't a muscle to contain. In the end, August risks everything—her savings, her pride, her whole heart—by publicly claiming both her craft and her love, and Theo walks away from his inheritance to build something new with her, proving that love chosen freely outlasts anything merely inherited.
about_author: Petra Sterling is the pen name of a former pastry chef turned novelist who spent a decade working in hotel kitchens before trading her piping bags for prose. She writes love stories about people who build things—cakes, businesses, lives—with their hands and then must learn to let someone in.

chapters.title: Three Missed Payments
chapters.summary: August's POV. August opens her café to a final notice from the bank and a morning of flawless, guarded routine—tempering chocolate, deflecting her sister's concern, refusing to feel the fear. Emotional beat: controlled desperation, the armor established.

chapters.title: The Man Who Orders the Same Thing
chapters.summary: August's POV. Theo Vance has been a quiet regular for months—black coffee, the same lemon tart, generous tips, no small talk. When his card declines and August covers it, an awkward conversation cracks the ice. Emotional beat: curiosity kindled beneath professional distance.

chapters.title: A Reunion Requires a Plus-One
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo confesses his family's centennial reunion at Vance House and the ultimatum from his father: arrive settled or lose standing in the family firm. He proposes a paid arrangement—August as his girlfriend for one weekend. Emotional beat: two liars recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: August's POV. August negotiates a fee that would clear her debt, drafting 'relationship rules' like a contract: no real feelings, no backstory questions, one weekend. Theo signs with a pen he leaves behind. Emotional beat: the thrill and dread of a deal that feels like a door opening.

chapters.title: Rehearsal
chapters.summary: August's POV. A practice date at her café—learning each other's tells, inventing how they met, Theo surprising her by actually listening. A near-kiss at closing time that both pretend didn't happen. Emotional beat: chemistry outpacing the script.

chapters.title: Vance House
chapters.summary: August's POV. Arrival at the estate: marble, portraits, and Theo's father, Richard, who inspects August like an acquisition. His grandmother, the formidable matriarch Eleanor, watches them with unsettling knowing. Emotional beat: August's invisibility strategy failing on arrival.

chapters.title: The Family Ledger
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo navigates his siblings' rivalries and learns his father is pushing to acquire the block of storefronts including August's café—using Theo as the face of the deal. Emotional beat: the first fracture between duty and conscience.

chapters.title: Dessert
chapters.summary: August's POV. August, cornered into contributing dessert, bakes her signature tart and the table falls silent with delight—Eleanor's gaze sharpening. Theo looks at her like the performance has stopped mattering. Emotional beat: seen for the first time, and terrified of it.

chapters.title: The Boathouse
chapters.summary: August's POV. Escaping the party, August and Theo talk by the water—real histories, her dead mother, his dead mother, the reasons they both hide. They kiss, breaking their own rule one night in. Emotional beat: surrender disguised as an exception.

chapters.title: Morning After, Rules Broken
chapters.summary: August's POV. August wakes in Theo's room and panics back into the contract, insisting it was a lapse. Eleanor finds her alone and offers a cryptic warning: 'The Vances buy things. Ask what he's buying.' Emotional beat: doubt planted in fertile soil.

chapters.title: The Acquisition
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo discovers the acquisition papers—his father's plan to raze the block for a flagship hotel, August's café included, with Theo's signature required as project lead. Emotional beat: horror and complicity; he knew the block was a target and never told her.

chapters.title: What She Doesn't Know
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo tries to stall the deal and quietly arrange an out for August's lease, telling himself it's protection, not deception. A board call forces him to present the acquisition favorably. Emotional beat: the corruption of power beginning its quiet work on him.

chapters.title: Home, and Wrong
chapters.summary: August's POV. Back at the café, August finds Theo distant and a developer's surveyor photographing her building. Her sister urges her to fight; August, trained to disappear, almost signs a lowball buyout offer. Emotional beat: old survival instincts versus a new, stubborn hope.

chapters.title: Eleanor's Invitation
chapters.summary: August's POV. Eleanor summons August to Vance House, reveals she knows the romance began as a contract—she read Theo's messages—and confesses she arranged their meeting to test whether Theo could love something he couldn't purchase. Emotional beat: humiliation and revelation braided together.

chapters.title: The Whole Truth, Half Too Late
chapters.summary: August's POV. August confronts Theo, who admits the acquisition, his signature, and that he'd been arranging her exit without her consent. August walks out, returning his payment uncashed. Emotional beat: the heart, lent out in pieces, recalled.

chapters.title: Empty Kitchen
chapters.summary: August's POV. A week of grief disguised as work. August bakes through the night for a catering job, and in the quiet admits she loves him—and that loving him means fighting for herself first. Emotional beat: the turn from heartbreak to agency.

chapters.title: The Boardroom Gambit
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo presents an alternative plan to the board—preserve the block as a culinary destination anchored by August's café, funded by restructuring his own inheritance stake. Richard threatens to cut him out entirely. Emotional bet: Theo choosing conscience over the crown.

chapters.title: Auction of the Block
chapters.summary: August's POV. The block goes to sealed bids. August, pooling savings, her sister's money, and a loan Eleanor quietly guarantees, submits a bid of her own. Emotional beat: the invisible woman making herself unignorable.

chapters.title: The Climax: Two Bids
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the estate's centennial gala, the winning bid is announced: August's, by a margin Theo secretly engineered by withdrawing his father's financing and resigning from the firm. Father and son collide publicly; August, learning of Theo's sacrifice, must decide whether love bought at his ruin can be freely hers. Emotional beat: everything risked at once.

chapters.title: The Whole Heart
chapters.summary: August's POV. August finds Theo packing his car outside Vance House, disinherited and unmoored. Instead of comforting him, she makes her own declaration—no contract, no rules, no pieces. She asks him to stay not because he lost everything but because she chooses him. Emotional beat: the risk of the whole heart, taken.

chapters.title: Rising
chapters.summary: August's POV. Months later: the café expands into the corner unit, the block saved, Theo learning to build without a name behind him. Eleanor visits as a customer, not a matriarch. Emotional beat: love and ambition no longer at war.

chapters.title: A Songbook for the Promise
chapters.summary: August's POV. One year on, at the café's anniversary, Theo proposes not with a ring but with a handwritten promise—terms and conditions rewritten: no expiration, no exit clause. August signs with the pen he once left behind. Emotional beat: the contract becomes a covenant; the song resolves.
